title: bmonitor · iPhone camera monitor for Mac, with Blackmagic Camera
description: Film with your iPhone's main camera and watch yourself on your Mac. bmonitor is a free iPhone camera monitor for the Blackmagic Camera app: live picture and sound over Wi-Fi, about 0.3 s behind, plus record, ISO, shutter and focus from the Mac.
hero_title:
Monitor your iPhone camera
from your Mac.
hero_sub: Film with the iPhone's main camera and watch yourself on the Mac that's already on your desk, in landscape or portrait. bmonitor monitors and remote-controls the free Blackmagic Camera app over Wi‑Fi, about 0.3 s behind.
hero_meta: Free and open source · macOS 14 or later · Apple Silicon and Intel · Public beta

features_title:
Readable from across the room.
Built to feel native.
feat_1_body: Recording, timecode, the active mic and the minutes left on the iPhone stay large in the top corners. A red border tells you you're rolling. For vertical video, safe areas show where Instagram, TikTok and Shorts cover the frame.
feat_2_body: Click anywhere on the video and the iPhone focuses there. Zoom, lens and stabilization are one click away too.
feat_3_body: ISO, shutter (speed or angle), white balance with light presets and tint, plus resolution, frame rate, codec and color space. The Mac shows the value the camera confirmed, not the one you asked for.
feat_4_body: The mic's name and an L/R meter in Blackmagic's own green, yellow and red. With an external mic, set its gain from the Mac. The camera's sound can play on the Mac, muted by default.
feat_5_body: I for ISO, S for shutter, W for white balance, ⌘R to record. Press ⌘/ to see them all.
setup_title:
Set it up once.
Then just open it.
setup_sub: After the first time, bmonitor finds the iPhone by itself.
step_1_body: Open the .dmg and drag bmonitor to Applications.
step_2_body: When the Mac asks to let bmonitor find devices on your local network, click Allow.
step_3_body: In Settings, turn on Remote Camera Control and use this iPhone as Remote Camera. In Network Access, turn on the HTTP server.
step_4_body: Same Wi‑Fi, Blackmagic Camera on the camera screen, auto-lock off. Open bmonitor.
a1: A Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later (Apple Silicon or Intel), an iPhone with the free Blackmagic Camera app, and both on the same Wi‑Fi network.
q2: Does it record on my Mac?
a2: The recording stays on the iPhone, in the quality you chose there. If you want a backup right away, turn on the copy next to the record button: each take is also saved on the Mac from the live stream, at the camera's resolution and about 8 Mb/s.
q3: How far behind real time is the video?
a3: About 0.3 s glass to glass, most of it on the iPhone side. Enough to check framing, focus and sound while you talk.
q4: What does it change on my iPhone?
a4: It adds a streaming platform called “Mac Monitor SRT” to Blackmagic Camera and makes it active while bmonitor is open. When you quit, it stops the stream and restores the platform you had before.
q5: Can I use more than one iPhone?
a5: One at a time. If there's more than one on the network, bmonitor asks which one to use.
a6: It's a public beta. It works every day on the author's setup, but so far it was tested on two Macs (macOS 26 and macOS 14) and one iPhone, so expect rough edges and report what you find.
q7: Is it made by Blackmagic Design?
a7: No. bmonitor is an independent project that talks to Blackmagic Camera through its documented remote API and live stream.
a8: Yes. Free and open source (MIT), with no ads, no account and no paid version. It collects nothing and only talks to the iPhone on your network. If it's useful to you, a coffee is welcome and never required.

q9: How do I see myself while filming with the iPhone's back camera?
a9: Put the iPhone on a tripod with the Blackmagic Camera app, open bmonitor on your Mac, and the Mac becomes your monitor: framing, focus, sound and recording status, readable from about 3 m. No clip-on screen to buy and no second iPhone or iPad.
q10: How do I monitor my iPhone camera on my Mac?
a10: Record with Blackmagic Camera on the iPhone and open bmonitor on the Mac, both on the same Wi‑Fi. You get the live picture and sound, and you can start recording and change ISO, shutter, white balance, focus, zoom and lens from the Mac. Continuity Camera is different: it turns the iPhone into a webcam for Mac apps and doesn't monitor a recording on the iPhone.
q11: How is this different from Blackmagic Camera on the Mac?
a11: Blackmagic Camera also runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later and can monitor a remote iPhone. It's the full iPad camera app on the Mac, and it can control several cameras at once. bmonitor does one job: a native Mac window with less delay in the author's test, the camera's sound on the Mac, portrait mode, status readable from 3 m and one key per control. It also runs on Intel Macs and macOS 14. See the full comparison.
feat_6_body: Turn the monitor to portrait with ⌘→ and frame Reels, TikTok and Shorts the way people will watch them.
